transcript.text: my washin mashine wont turn on at all no lights nothin

A washing machine with absolutely no lights or response when you press the button usually means it isn't getting electricity at all. The most common cause is simply that the socket has no power, the plug has worked loose, or a nearby switched fuse (spur) has been turned off. 1. Check the socket: Plug a lamp or phone charger into the same socket to confirm it actually has power. If nothing works there, check your home's fuse box or any switched spur near the washing machine to make sure it is turned on.
2. Check the plug and lead: Ensure the washing machine's plug is pushed firmly all the way into the wall socket. Look along the cable for any obvious damage or pinching. If the socket is dead, fixing that will likely solve your problem immediately.
the kettle works in the kitchen so other sockets are ok. i cant reach the washing machine plug tho its behind the unit, its built in. whats a spur?

A spur is a small fused switch on the wall (usually near the appliance) that isolates the power to it. It's common for these to be switched off accidentally, especially after moving furniture. Since you can't reach the plug behind the machine and other sockets are working, we need to check if the washing machine has its own dedicated supply or if the plug has simply vibrated loose over time. 1. Look around the wall near where the machine is for a small switch with a red light or a fuse box cover - that's a spur. Is it switched on?
2. If there isn't one, try carefully pulling the washing machine forward just an inch or two to see if you can wiggle the plug back into the socket firmly. Let me know what you find.

ok i looked and theres a row of switches above the worktop, one says washer and its OFF. my flatmate must of turned it off when she was cleaning. i turned it back on and the machine lights up now and works!

That's excellent news. It sounds like the washing machine was simply isolated by that spur switch rather than having a mechanical fault. To stop this from happening again, you might want to put a small sticky label on that specific switch so your flatmate knows it controls the washer and shouldn't be turned off during cleaning. Is there anything else I can help you with today?
